title: Can a 30-minute AI prompt routine earn you $500 a month? My real-world test
excerpt: I ran a short daily AI routine for a month and tracked every dollar. Here is what sold, what flopped, and whether I would do it again.
metaDescription: Honest month-long test of a 30-minute daily AI prompt routine for side income. Tools, workflow, real numbers, and what I would change.
author: Ali Hamza
coverImageAlt: Person writing notes beside a laptop
body:
## I was skeptical

Every week someone claims a tiny AI habit can mint side income. I already full-time freelancing. I did not want another fake productivity ritual. So I ran a clean experiment: **30 minutes a day, four weeks, sell something small, track net cash after tools.**

## Rules I set for myself

- Cap work at 30 minutes on weekdays only.
- Keep tool cost under $50/month.
- Sell on Gumroad only (no ads).
- Log revenue and costs in a simple sheet.

## The stack

- **ChatGPT** for outlines and short product copy.
- **Midjourney** (basic) for cover images.
- **Zapier free tier** to push a Google Sheet row into a Gumroad draft.

Nothing fancy. If it needed a new platform, I skipped it.

## What the 30 minutes looked like

1. **10 min:** Ask ChatGPT for five niche ideas plus a short teaser for each (one industry per day).
2. **10 min:** Generate one thumbnail in Midjourney and pick the least ugly option.
3. **10 min:** Drop title, teaser, image URL, and $5 price into the sheet so Zapier could draft the product.

I shipped **20 products** in four weeks.

## What actually moved

A few low-price checklists sold again and again:

- Freelance pricing cheat sheet
- Quick SEO checklist for bloggers
- Remote work burnout guide

Most other drafts sat at zero. After ~$45 in AI plans and a bit of Zapier, **net was under $500**. Useful side cash. Not a salary.

## Time math

About **12.5 hours** across the month. Net worked out near **$35-$40/hour**. Fine for autopilot filler. Not worth killing client work for.

## What I tried that failed

- Batching a whole week of prompts in one sitting made the copy generic.
- Raising the price to $10 cut conversions in half.

Small price, clear micro-problem, high volume worked better for me.

## If you copy this

- Start with one niche you already understand.
- Ship daily for two weeks before you judge the idea.
- Subtract tool cost before you call it profit.
- Stop if it steals energy from paid clients.

## FAQ

**Do I need design skills for Midjourney?**
No. Describe the idea clearly and pick the best frame.

**Can I use another store than Gumroad?**
Yes. Point Zapier (or Make) at Payhip, Lemon Squeezy, or Stripe. The routine stays the same.

## Bottom line

A tight 30-minute AI routine can fund a small buffer. It will not replace freelance income. Treat it as a measured experiment, not a miracle, and keep the numbers honest.
